newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SUEZ, LYONNAISE MERGER UNLIKELY. [CORRECTED 09:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SUEZ, LYONNAISE MERGER UNLIKELY. [CORRECTED 09:55 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to replace all references to Cie. Generale des Eaux with Lyonnaise des Eaux)
A merger between French holding companies Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux was unlikely, the head of Belgian banking and insurance company Fortis AG was quoted as saying on Friday.

"From the contacts I have had with Suez, (a merger) does not really seem to be on the agenda. There aren't any lawyers or bankers working on it at the moment," Fortis AG chairman Maurice Lippens told Belgian newspaper L'Echo in an interview.
Fortis AG is 20-percent owned by Societe Generale de Belgique , Suez's main asset. Fortis has a 12 percent stake in SGB.
SGB recently increased its stake in Belgian utility group Tractebel , heightening speculation about an eventual Suez/Lyonnaise or Tractebel/Lyonnaise merger.
Lippens said, however, the merger plan was like the Loch Ness monster: it surfaces from time to time, but no one is ever quite sure if they have seen it.
"(Suez CEO) Gerard Mestrallet is still convinced that the financial services sector offers the best prospects for growth. On this he differs with Albert Frere," Lippens said.

Belgian financier Albert Frere, the head of Groupe Bruxelles Lambert and numerous other holding companies, has recently built up a small minority interest in Suez and has been invited to join its board.
